candidates.name: Party of Farmers, Traders and Independents

elections.notes: Votes and shares are the article's table (shares of 961,498 valid votes); turnout is the table's, from its electorate and ballots. The article doesn't say what its national votes column counts. Voters cast one vote per seat in their canton, and the article's by-constituency table counts those party votes, which are much larger than the national figures. Others: Liberal Socialist Party, and the table's other parties. Only men could vote; the 1971 article says that was the first federal election in which women could vote. Region winners are the party with the most votes in each canton, from the article's by-constituency table (party votes, cited to the Federal Gazette); Jura was part of the canton of Bern until 1979, so it has no winner of its own and Bern's covers both; no winner for GL (elected unopposed), SH (elected unopposed).

candidates.name: Party of Farmers, Traders and Independents

elections.notes: Seats are the council's party composition after all rounds, as the article's table gives it (Nohlen & Stöver); the table has no votes. Members are elected canton by canton, mostly by majority vote with run-offs, so the date is the National Council's polling day. Jura had no seats until its first election in 1979. The article notes that in several cantons the members were chosen by the cantonal parliaments. Others: Other parties (2). Only men could vote; the 1971 article says that was the first federal election in which women could vote. The article has no results by canton for this council, so no region winners.
